voice.text: Will tomorrow be sunny, or stormy? [pause] Can anyone know before it happens? Tap your guess.
Forecasters use tools. <emphasis>The thermometer measures how warm the air is.</emphasis> The red line climbs on a hot day. [pause] The tool only measures — it never makes the weather.
<emphasis>The rain gauge is a measuring cup for the sky.</emphasis> Rain falls in, and the marks show how much rain fell.
<emphasis>The windsock fills up and points.</emphasis> It shows which way the wind blows, and how hard.

A junior forecaster measures every day, and <emphasis>records</emphasis> it. Each sunny day gets one sun picture. Stack the pictures — and the week becomes a <emphasis>pictograph!</emphasis> [pause] Now you can SEE the pattern: lots of sun, some rain.

The pattern helps you <emphasis>predict</emphasis>: dark clouds piling up, wind rising — a storm is probably coming. So you <emphasis>prepare!</emphasis> Charge the flashlight. Bring toys inside. Stay in where it's safe. [pause] Knowing early keeps us ready.
Time for forecaster training! [pause] Match each tool to its job, then read the weather chart. Tap your answer.
Training complete, junior forecaster! [pause] Now show what you know.
Which job does the thermometer do?
Which job does the rain gauge do?
Which job does the windsock do?
Look at the chart. Which kind of day happened most?
How many rainy days were there?
How many more sunny days than rainy days?
Which kind of day happened the fewest?
The chart shows storm clouds building. What is a smart way to get ready?
Yes! [pause] The thermometer measures how warm — it never makes the weather.
Yes! [pause] The rain gauge catches rain, and its marks show how much fell.
Yes! [pause] The windsock fills and points — that is the wind talking.
Yes! [pause] The sunny row has the most pictures — four!
Yes! [pause] Two rain pictures — two rainy days.
Yes! [pause] Four sunny take away two rainy leaves two more.
Yes! [pause] Cloudy has just one picture — the fewest. The chart tells us all of this!
Yes! [pause] Predicting lets you prepare — flashlight ready, safe inside.
Not quite. Tools only MEASURE the weather. [pause] They never make it.
Not quite. You CAN know — the recorded pattern gives clues about tomorrow.
Not quite. The pictures are data! [pause] Each picture counts one real day.
Not quite. Count the pictures in each row — each picture is one day.
Not quite. A storm is coming — forecasters prepare, and stay safe.
Not quite. Look again at the tool's job.
Not quite. Look again.
Which tool tells you how warm it is?
The thermometer shows a hot day. Did the thermometer MAKE it hot?
Look at the chart. How many sunny days were in the week?
Why record the weather every single day?
The pattern says a storm is coming tonight. What do you do?
<soft>You're a junior forecaster!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the tools once more.
Lesson done! Now go make a paper pictograph of your own weather journal, with your parent.
